title: Daswandh in the code
hook: giving a tenth of earnings for the Guru's cause

segments.voice: Yesterday, the code's refusals: no caste, no charms, no omens, one light in everyone. Your line was no lucky days. Which little superstition did you skip, and did the day carry on? Day one thousand two hundred sixty-five.

Payday. The money lands, and before it does anything else, it gets sorted. Rent here. Groceries there. Something for the phone bill, something for the car. Every household has its own version of that sorting, on paper or in an app or in someone's head. Now add one more pile to the front of the line, set aside before rent, not after the fun. Not a tip for whatever is left over, but a share taken first and given away. Sikhs have a plain name for that share, and it has nothing to do with leftovers.
screen: `PAYDAY, SORTED INTO PILES.` → `ONE MORE PILE, AT THE FRONT.` → `A SHARE GIVEN FIRST.`

segments.voice: Daswandh means a tenth part. In Sikh teaching, it is a tenth of one's earnings, given for the Guru's cause, and it belongs to the way of life the code sets out for a Sikh. Three things are worth noticing. First, what it comes out of. Daswandh is tied to earnings, to honest work. Sikh teaching joins remembering the Name, earning honestly, and sharing what you have. Daswandh sits where earning and sharing meet. Guru Nanak puts it in one line, on Ang twelve hundred forty-five, in paraphrase: the one who eats what they earn by their own work and gives some of it away from their own hand, that one recognizes the path. Not a gift from someone else's pocket. From your own hand. Second, where it goes. The Guru's cause is wide. It can fund the langar, where anyone can sit and eat. It can keep gurdwaras open, support schools, and pay for relief when disaster strikes. Some Sikhs give it in money, others give part of it in time, serving in the kitchen or teaching children. Communities differ on how strictly to count. Third, the measure. A tenth is concrete. It's small enough to live with and large enough to notice. That is the point. Giving whatever is left over depends on mood. A tenth, set aside first, turns sharing from a feeling into a habit, and the habit into a quiet partnership with everyone the langar feeds.
screen: `DASWANDH: A TENTH PART.` · `FROM HONEST EARNINGS.` · `FOR THE GURU'S CAUSE.` · `A MEASURE THAT MAKES A HABIT.` · then, large: `A TENTH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: give something this week. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind what came to you lately, money, time or skill. Don't do the math yet. Just picture setting a share of it apart, first, before the other piles. Then ask where it could go. A food bank, a neighbor, a gurdwara kitchen, an hour of help to someone stretched thin. Choose one, and choose a day this week. Hold that plan quietly until the bell. If you pray, you can offer it with the word Waheguru. The bell holds the time.
Daswandh in the code. A tenth part of honest earnings, given for the Guru's cause, set aside first. Today's word.
Your line: a tenth. Today, before you spend anything, set aside a small share of it in your mind, or in a jar, for someone else. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-five.
